e-12760.problem:
Consider the following sets:

$$
A = \{ 2n \mid n \in \mathbb{N}\}, \qquad
B = \left\{  2^{-n} \mid n \in \mathbb {N}\right\}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A = \{ 2, 4, 6,\ldots \}$

- $A \cap B = \emptyset$

- $A$ and $B$ are disjoint
e-12760.worked_solution:
Two sets $A$ and $B$ are *disjoint* if they have no element in common, i.e., their intersection is empty:

$$
A \cap B = \emptyset
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets.

- Statement I is true.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={2n∣n\in N} \\  & ={2(1),2(2),2(3),…} \\  & ={2,4,6,…}\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is true. First, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={{2}^{-n}∣n\in N} \\  & ={{2}^{-1},{2}^{-2},{2}^{-3},…} \\  & ={\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{8},…}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the intersection of $A$ and $B$ is 

$$
A \cap B = \{ 2, 4, 6, \ldots \} \cap \left\{\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{1}{8},\ldots \right\} = \emptyset.
$$

- Statement III is true. Since the intersection is empty, the two sets are disjoint.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II and III."

e-12761.knowledge_point: Finding the Disjoint Union of Non-Overlapping Sets
e-12761.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets $\{ -1, 1, \sqrt{5} \}$ and $\{ v, w \}.$
e-12761.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are disjoint since

$$
\{ -1, 1, \sqrt{5} \} \cap \{ v, w \} = \emptyset.
$$

Therefore, the disjoint union is simply the union:

$$
\begin{aligned}{-1,1,\sqrt{5}}⊔{v,w} & ={-1,1,\sqrt{5}}\cup {v,w} \\  & ={-1,1,\sqrt{5},v,w}\end{aligned}
$$

e-12762.knowledge_point: Finding the Disjoint Union of Overlapping Sets
e-12762.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets $A_1 = \{ 7,8 \}$ and $A_2 = \{ 2,4,8 \}.$
e-12762.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
\{ 7,8 \} \cap \{ 2,4,8 \} = \{ 8 \} \neq \emptyset.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}={(7,1),(8,1)} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}={(2,2),(4,2),(8,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & ={7,8}⊔{2,4,8} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & ={(7,1),(8,1)}\cup {(2,2),(4,2),(8,2)} \\  & ={(7,1),(8,1),(2,2),(4,2),(8,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are disjoint since

$$
{3,6,9}\cap {p,q,r}=∅.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{3,6,9}⊔{p,q,r} & ={3,6,9}\cup {p,q,r} \\  & ={3,6,9,p,q,r}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}={3,\pi ,4}$ and ${A}_{2}={-1,4}.$
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
{3,\pi ,4}\cap {-1,4}={4}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1)} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}={(-1,2),(4,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & ={3,\pi ,4}⊔{-1,4} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & ={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1)}\cup {(-1,2),(4,2)} \\  & ={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1),(-1,2),(4,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}={3,\pi ,4}$ and ${A}_{2}={-1,4}.$
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
{3,\pi ,4}\cap {-1,4}={4}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1)} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}={(-1,2),(4,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & ={3,\pi ,4}⊔{-1,4} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & ={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1)}\cup {(-1,2),(4,2)} \\  & ={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1),(-1,2),(4,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the disjoint union of the sets A1={△,◻,♣} and A2={♠,♣}.

a
{(△,1),(◻,1),(♣,1),(♠,2),(♣,2)}
b
{△,◻,♠}
c
{△,◻,♣,♠}

{(△,♠),(◻,♠)}
e
{(△,♠),(△,♣),(◻,♠),(◻,♣),(♣,♠)}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that the sets are overlapping since {△,◻,♣}∩{♠,♣}={♣}≠∅.

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows: A1→A1∗={(△,1),(◻,1),(♣,1)}A2→A2∗={(♠,2),(♣,2)}

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets: A1⊔A2={△,◻,♣}⊔{♠,♣}=A1∗∪A2∗={(△,1),(◻,1),(♣,1)}∪{(♠,2),(♣,2)}={(△,1),(◻,1),(♣,1),(♠,2),(♣,2)}

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Disjoint Union of Overlapping Sets
content.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}={△,◻,♣}$ and ${A}_{2}={♠,♣}.$
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
{△,◻,♣}\cap {♠,♣}={♣}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}={(△,1),(◻,1),(♣,1)} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}={(♠,2),(♣,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & ={△,◻,♣}⊔{♠,♣} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & ={(△,1),(◻,1),(♣,1)}\cup {(♠,2),(♣,2)} \\  & ={(△,1),(◻,1),(♣,1),(♠,2),(♣,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}={a,b,c}$ and ${A}_{2}={b,c,d}.$
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
{a,b,c}\cap {b,c,d}={b,c}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}={(a,1),(b,1),(c,1)} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}={(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & ={a,b,c}⊔{b,c,d} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & ={(a,1),(b,1),(c,1)}\cup {(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)} \\  & ={(a,1),(b,1),(c,1),(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}={a,b,c}$ and ${A}_{2}={b,c,d}.$
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
{a,b,c}\cap {b,c,d}={b,c}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}={(a,1),(b,1),(c,1)} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}={(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & ={a,b,c}⊔{b,c,d} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & ={(a,1),(b,1),(c,1)}\cup {(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)} \\  & ={(a,1),(b,1),(c,1),(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}={p,q,r}$ and ${A}_{2}={r,t}.$
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
{p,q,r}\cap {r,t}={r}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}={(p,1),(q,1),(r,1)} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}={(r,2),(t,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & ={p,q,r}⊔{r,t} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & ={(p,1),(q,1),(r,1)}\cup {(r,2),(t,2)} \\  & ={(p,1),(q,1),(r,1),(r,2),(t,2)}\end{aligned}
$$
